tree.onlyNodeGone: Deleting the only node leaves nothing: the tree is empty.
tree.unlinkLeft: Set {{parent}}'s left link to nothing. {{x}} is gone.
tree.unlinkRight: Set {{parent}}'s right link to nothing. {{x}} is gone.
tree.oneChildRoot: cur holds x = {{x}}. It has one child, {{child}}, and no parent: it is the root.
tree.oneChild: cur holds x = {{x}}. It has one child, {{child}}: point the parent's link at that child.
tree.newRoot: The root has no parent, so deleting it makes its child, {{child}}, the new root.
tree.relinkLeft: Point {{parent}}'s left link at {{child}}. Its subtree moves up with it, and {{x}} is gone.
tree.relinkRight: Point {{parent}}'s right link at {{child}}. Its subtree moves up with it, and {{x}} is gone.
tree.twoChildren: cur holds x = {{x}}. It has two children, {{left}} and {{right}}: find the successor, the smallest value in the right subtree.
tree.noLeft: {{value}} has no left child, so it is the successor.
tree.stepRight: Step right once: successor = {{succ}}, successor's parent = {{parent}}.
tree.stepLeft: {{parent}} has a left child, so step left: successor = {{succ}}, successor's parent = {{parent}}.
tree.copy: Copy {{value}} into cur: the node that held {{x}} now holds {{value}}. Now remove the successor node.
tree.succDirect: The successor is cur's own right child, so set cur.right to the successor's right child, {{right}}.
tree.succDeepNone: The old {{value}} node has no children, so {{parent}}'s left link now points at {{right}}.
tree.succDeepOne: The old {{value}} node has one child, {{right}}, so {{parent}}'s left link now points at {{right}}.
tree.printEmpty: The tree is empty, so print an empty line.
tree.printPreorder: Print the tree in preorder: the root, then the left subtree, then the right subtree: {{order}}.
tree.atMost_one: Enter at most {{count}} number, so the tree fits.
tree.atMost_other: Enter at most {{count}} numbers, so the tree fits.
tree.repeated: The values must be distinct: {{value}} appears more than once.
tree.memberInvalid: {{name}} must be a whole number, one of the values in the tree.
tree.memberMissing: {{name}} = {{value}} is not in the tree. Use one of: {{values}}.

height.hint: 0 to {{nodes}} distinct whole numbers from -{{max}} to {{max}}, in insertion order. Leave it empty for an empty tree. (The problem allows up to 1000 values from -1000000 to 1000000.)

lca.hint: 2 to {{nodes}} distinct whole numbers from -{{max}} to {{max}}, in insertion order, then p and q: two values from the tree, in either order, and they may be equal. (The problem allows up to 1000 values from -1000000 to 1000000.)

delete.hint: 1 to {{nodes}} distinct whole numbers from -{{max}} to {{max}}, in insertion order, then x: the value to delete, one of the values in the tree. (The problem allows up to 1000 values from -1000000 to 1000000.)

height.path: on the insert path or popped

delete.focus: just inserted, successor or moved up

tree.label: Root {{root}}. Nodes: {{nodes}}.
tree.region: Tree drawing, scrolls sideways when it is wider than the screen
tree.stackTitle: Stack of (value, depth) pairs (top on the right)
tree.legendPathHeight: On the insert path, or already popped
tree.legendFocusDelete: Just inserted, the successor, or the child that moved up
tree.legendEdge: Link used or changed in this step

twoPointer.start: Put L on the first character and R on the last.
twoPointer.swap: Swap {{a}} and {{b}} at positions {{left}} and {{right}}, then move both pointers inward.
twoPointer.meet: L and R meet at position {{position}}. The middle character, {{c}}, stays where it is.
twoPointer.differ: {{a}} and {{b}} differ, so stop here. Not a palindrome.
twoPointer.match: {{a}} and {{b}} match, so move both pointers inward.
twoPointer.single: A single character reads the same both ways. Palindrome.
twoPointer.meetMiddle: L and R meet at the middle character, {{c}}, and every pair matched. Palindrome.
twoPointer.crossed: L and R have crossed, and every pair matched. Palindrome.

palindrome.hint: 1 to {{max}} lowercase letters a to z, no spaces or capitals (the same rule as the problem).
palindrome.patternError: Use only lowercase letters a to z, with no spaces.

twoPointer.label: Text: "{{text}}".
twoPointer.pointers: L, R: left and right pointers. Small numbers: indices.
twoPointer.pointersSpace: L, R: left and right pointers. Small numbers: indices. ␣ is a space.

reverse.hint: 1 to {{max}} characters: letters, digits and single spaces, with no space at the start or end (the same rule as the problem).
reverse.patternError: Use only letters, digits and single spaces, with no space at the start or end.

twoSum.start: Start with an empty map. Look for two positions that add up to {{target}}.
twoSum.question: Position {{i}}, value {{value}}: the partner would be {{target}} - {{term}} = {{partner}}. Is {{partner}} in the map?
twoSum.yes: Yes, at position {{at}}. The answer is {{at}} {{i}}.
twoSum.replaced: {{value}} was already in the map, so its position becomes {{i}}.
twoSum.targetInvalid: Enter the target as one whole number.
twoSum.noPair: No pair adds up to {{target}}. The problem guarantees exactly one.
twoSum.manyPairs_one: {{count}} pairs add up to {{target}} (positions {{positions}}). The problem allows exactly one.
twoSum.manyPairs_other: {{count}} pairs add up to {{target}} (positions {{positions}}). The problem allows exactly one.
twoSum.label: Numbers: {{values}}.
twoSum.hint: 2 to {{max}} whole numbers from -{{limit}} to {{limit}}, and a target. As in the problem, exactly one pair of positions must add up to the target.

warmup.start: The grader writes "{{input}}" to standard input and starts your program.
warmup.prompt: Your program prints "{{prompt}}". No person reads it: it goes to standard output, like everything printed.
warmup.read: Your program reads the text "{{text}}" from standard input. It is text, not a number yet.
warmup.convert: It converts the text "{{text}}" to the integer {{value}}.
warmup.passed: The grader compares "{{actual}}" with the expected "{{expected}}": passed.
warmup.verdictExtraLine: Failed: the output has an extra line
warmup.failed_one: The grader compares the output, {{shown}} on {{count}} lines, with the expected "{{expected}}". They differ. {{verdict}}.
warmup.failed_other: The grader compares the output, {{shown}} on {{count}} lines, with the expected "{{expected}}". They differ. {{verdict}}.
warmup.invalid: Enter one whole number from -{{limit}} to {{limit}}.
warmup.hint: A whole number from -{{limit}} to {{limit}}, as in the problem. The answer, 2 * n, still fits in a 32-bit int.
